In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the angular excitation of a particle in the potential of a given sign is a good approximation to the fine structure of a particle in that potential.
, in all cases, the angular excitations of the particle are the most sensitive to the potential.
the fine structure of a spin-1/2 particle in an external field is a consequence of the fine structure of the free particle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the angular excitations of particles submitted to potentials with a laplacians of given signs are a very rich source of inequalities on the fine structure and on hyperfine splittings, on the wave function at the center, and on the binding energies, and that they can be successfully applied in atomic and particle physics.

we have obtained new results on the fine structure of the hydrogen atom, the Lamb shift, the hyperfine structure, and the fine and hyperfine structure of the positronium, and that we have obtained inequalities on ionization energy and on the 1S wave function at the center of an atom.

, in the case of the hydrogen atom, the inequalities we obtained are more accurate and more general than previous ones, and that the inequalities we obtained for muonic atoms are more accurate and general than those of the literature.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the fine structure of atomic systems is determined by the laplacian of the potential.
the sign of the laplacian plays a crucial role in the determination of fine and hyperfine structure of atomic systems.

inequalities on the fine structure constant, on quark masses, and on the fine splitting of angular excitations can be derived from the knowledge of the ground state energy, the 1s function at the origin, and the ground state wave function of the particle in a given potential.
